method: Inspected labelled thirteen-parent contact sheet at224×280 per portrait. No actual suspect requiring enlargement found. Parent portrait, command, teaching, lookout and specimen-examination poses were judged by their depicted action rather than requiring every subject to look down.

rows.title: Alexander the Great
rows.reason: Head follows the commanding riding direction; neck joins naturally to the armoured torso.

rows.title: Aristotle
rows.reason: Frontal teaching gesture addresses the viewer/listeners; no strained head rotation.

rows.title: Euclid
rows.reason: Slight downward three-quarter head over the geometry table; neck is aligned with shoulders.

rows.title: Lysippos
rows.reason: Raised chin follows the tall sculpture in front/right; looking upward is justified by the subject.

rows.title: Pytheas of Massalia
rows.reason: Gaze follows the seaward horizon; normal lookout posture.

rows.title: Menander
rows.reason: Moderate head turn addresses the stage gathering; suitable speaking/storytelling pose.

rows.title: Demetrius the Besieger
rows.reason: Raised commanding gaze with an indicating arm; head/neck remain plausibly joined to the torso.

rows.title: Theophrastus
rows.reason: Head and eyes examine the raised botanical specimen.

rows.title: Zeno of Citium
rows.reason: Head addresses the visible student; open-hand teaching gesture supports the gaze.

rows.title: Ptolemy I Soter
rows.reason: Modest outward statesman portrait gaze; hands rest on documents rather than a precision task.

rows.title: Cleomenes of Naucratis
rows.reason: Head and eyes inspect the raised grain sample; neck inclination suits the examination.

rows.title: Nearchus
rows.reason: Outward lookout gaze suits the shipboard navigator role; no neck defect.

rows.title: Eumenes of Cardia
rows.reason: Slight outward portrait gaze while holding a scroll; no extreme head/shoulder rotation.
